title: Tenant-aware roles and authorization contracts for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current RBAC model is flat and conflates tenant boundaries, role intent, and admin policies. This causes ambiguous permissions across Dedicated and Private deployments, surprising privilege escalation paths, and noisy audit trails that are hard to attribute to a tenant or an admin action.

Goal: Design a tenant-aware role model and an explicit authorization contract that: (1) defines resource hierarchy and canonical scopes, (2) produces a deterministic permission resolution algorithm for request-time checks and query filters, (3) integrates with SSO/SAML role assertions and audit logging, and (4) supports progressive migration with feature flags and fallback to v1 semantics.

Deliverables:
- Resource hierarchy document (tenant -> workspace -> project -> model endpoint -> route) with canonical scope names.
- Permission matrix CSV mapping atomic actions (read_tokens, generate, manage_kv_cache, bind_roles, view_audit_log) to roles and scopes.
- Scope resolution algorithm (explicit precedence rules for tenant-scoped vs global admin roles).
- Policy for roleset inheritance and isolation for Dedicated / Private deployments.
- Audit logging schema addendum for RBAC v2 (fields required to attribute tenant, principal, role_version, scope_resolution_path).
- Mapping strategy for SAML attributes / OIDC groups to Redwood roles with verification hooks.
- Migration plan with canary rollout steps, runtime feature flags, and compatibility endpoints for SDKs.

Design summary:
- Resource hierarchy: canonical path format: tenant:{tenant_id}/workspace:{workspace_id}/project:{project_id}/endpoint:{endpoint_id}/route:{route_id}. All scopes are defined at one of these levels; implicit child inheritance is opt-in and recorded.
- Roles: split into three orthogonal axes: operational roles (view-*, manage-*), data roles (embed-*, generate-*, view-data), and admin roles (tenant-admin, security-admin, billing-admin). Roles are namespaced by tenant when created in a tenant context; global roles exist only for cross-tenant ops and require explicit global approval.
- Permission matrix: permissions are atomic and boolean; composite permissions are created by role definitions. The canonical source of truth is a CSV in the RBAC repo and seeded during migration.
- Scope resolution: algorithm orders explicit grant > role membership > implicit inheritance > global fallback. For each request we evaluate (1) principal explicit grants, (2) role-based grants at the exact scope, (3) inherited role grants from parent scopes (if inheritance flag set), (4) global role grants. The first match to allow/deny wins; deny is always precedence when explicit.
- Audit integration: every decision emits a structured audit event containing: principal_id, principal_type, role_version, evaluated_scopes (ordered list), decision, request_trace_id, matched_policy_id. These fields are required for downstream regressions and SLO investigations.
- SSO/SAML mapping: support declarative role assertions via SAML Attributes and OIDC group claims. Mapping table lives in tenant configuration and must be signed by tenant-admin. Unmapped assertions fall back to read-only 'external-user' with no admin privileges.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict inheritance reduces admin friction but increases risk of privilege creep; we propose opt-in inheritance per role with an audit-only mode initially.
- Evaluating entire parent chain at request-time ensures correctness but has performance cost; we'll implement a cached flattened policy per principal scope to reduce lookups and invalidate on role changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- AuthZ decisions for 95% of requests are served from cache with average additional latency <1ms.
- Audit events contain required fields and are searchable by tenant_id and role_version.
- SAML/OIDC mapping supports at least two identity providers in a tenant config and profile tests pass.
- Migration tool can convert at least 90% of existing v1 roles into v2 rolesets automatically and logs ambiguous cases for manual review.

open_questions: What is the canonical TTL for flattened policy cache and how to surface cache misses in traces?
How should we represent third-party collaborators who need temporary cross-tenant access?
Do we provide a managed UI for tenant-admins to author SAML mapping or require tenant-provided mapping files?
decisions: Use ordered evaluated_scopes list in audit events to make policy resolution deterministic.
Inheritance is opt-in per role and recorded in the role definition; default is no inheritance.
Deny rules are prioritized over allow and explicit grants trump inherited grants.
